entity-75a6bc4c.name: Tim Hammond
entity-75a6bc4c.description:
Tim Hammond ([born Tim Sally](http://circumcisionharm.org/hammond%20cv.htm#Why)) is a grassroots human rights activist, genital autonomy pioneer, organizer, filmmaker, researcher, writer, and archivist who has dedicated nearly fifty years to social change movements. As a teenager conscientiously opposed to fighting in Vietnam, he wrote copious letters to Congress urging an immediate end to the war.

Tim has been committed to Congressional passage of the U.S. Peace Tax Fund Bill, which would redirect the military portion of one's taxes (currently 50% of every dollar spent by the U.S. government) toward life-sustaining human services. He was active in raising public consciousness about women's rights and the need for the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA).

In 1987, Tim was among hundreds of men and women arrested on the steps of the U.S. Supreme Court in civil disobedience to protest its decision in *Bowers v. Hardwick* upholding states' rights to legislate private sexual behavior among consenting adults in their own home (a decision the Court ultimately reversed in 2003). He was also a member of the Children's Rights Network of Amnesty International/USA and a member of the National Organization on Male Sexual Victimization (now MaleSurvivor.org).

### Why the Name Change?
In the late 1980s, when Tim (under his birth name, Tim Sally) began publicly denouncing infant male circumcision as a human rights violation, those who vehemently disagreed would search for his phone number and address in the San Francisco telephone directory. They constantly phoned and wrote to harass him with unfounded charges that he was "antisemitic" or a "pervert" for being "interested in little boys' penises." Tim adopted the surname of his first partner to shield his personal life and family from such reactionaries.

### Movement Building & Empirical Harm Research
Recognizing a critical void in medical and human rights discourse regarding the lifelong trauma of non-therapeutic infant surgery, Tim founded the National Organization to Halt the Abuse and Routine Mutilation of Males ([NOHARMM](http://noharmm.org/)) in 1992 and co-founded the National Organization of Restoring Men ([NORM](http://norm.org/)) in 1989. In 1993, he served as Survey Coordinator of *Awakenings: A Preliminary Poll of Circumcised Men*, the first landmark grassroots investigation into the physical, sexual, and psychological outcomes of infant circumcision (published in the *British Journal of Urology International* in 1999). In 1995, he executive-produced *Whose Body, Whose Rights?*, a 56-minute documentary accepted into the U.S. Library of Congress and the American Archives of Public Broadcasting.

### Legal Impact Litigation: GALDEF
In 2022, Tim founded and serves as President of the **[Genital Autonomy Legal Defense and Education Fund (GALDEF)](https://www.galdef.org/)** to organize and train legal professionals to become successful with impact litigation securing the bodily integrity and genital autonomy of children in the United States. Through GALDEF, Tim also spearheads educational series for clinicians and the World Association for Sexual Health (WAS).

### Archival Legacy
Decades of Tim's historic activist materials are preserved in the **Tim Hammond Genital Autonomy Advocacy Archives (MS 1205)** at the University of Massachusetts Amherst Special Collections, and the **Tim Sally LGBTQ+ Archives: Gay Rights & Intactivism Collection** at the Rochester (NY) Public Library.

entity-48e3c78b.name: Genital Autonomy Legal Defense and Education Fund (GALDEF)
entity-48e3c78b.description:
The **Genital Autonomy Legal Defense and Education Fund (GALDEF)** was founded in 2022 by veteran human rights activist and researcher **Tim Hammond**. Operating as a premier non-profit legal advocacy organization, GALDEF is dedicated to organizing, educating, and training legal professionals to achieve successful constitutional, civil, and tort impact litigation securing the bodily integrity and genital autonomy of children in the United States, particularly boys.

GALDEF works to overcome historical judicial deferral to parental tradition and clinical non-intervention by equipping litigators with robust empirical microdata on physical and psychological harm, bioethical jurisprudence, and 14th Amendment Equal Protection arguments. In addition to direct legal strategy and amicus support, GALDEF produces clinician educational curricula in partnership with organizations like the **World Association for Sexual Health (WAS)**, instructing medical providers on proper penile prepuce anatomy, biomechanics, and therapeutic approaches for circumcision harm.

entity-b10781ea.name: Medium
entity-b10781ea.tagline: Open digital publishing platform where independent researchers, cultural critics, and advocates publish long-form essays and investigative commentary.
entity-b10781ea.description: Medium is an open digital publishing platform widely used by independent researchers, journalists, and cultural essayists. Within the genital autonomy movement, writers and bioethicists frequently utilize Medium to publish long-form investigations, personal narratives, and cultural critiques outside conventional academic paywalls.

entity-885dd727.name: Substack
entity-885dd727.tagline: Independent publishing network and newsletter platform widely utilized by genital autonomy researchers and investigative writers, including The Accidental Intactivist.
entity-885dd727.description: Substack is an independent newsletter and publication network that provides a direct-to-reader publishing infrastructure. In the bodily integrity movement, Substack has become a primary medium for ongoing empirical reporting, legal case analysis (such as *Hadachek v. Oregon*), and serialized investigative projects including *The Accidental Intactivist's Guide*.
